faq: What does this tool calculate?
Pace per mile from pace per kilometre: min/km × 1.609344, shown as minutes and seconds per mile.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes, in your browser as you type — nothing is uploaded, no account exists to upload to.
How accurate is the result?
Exact to the definition of the mile; rounding to the nearest second is the only approximation, and it is shown, not hidden.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Your legs are the route; this is unit conversion for their pace.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Unrelated to pace, but worth knowing on the run: your watch's distance is the path you took, which is the honest one for pace.
Why multiply and not divide?
A mile contains 1.609344 kilometres, so covering one takes 1.609344 times as long at the same speed. The pace number grows with the unit.
The reverse direction?
Divide by 1.609344 — the Minutes per Mile to Minutes per KM Converter is organised for exactly that.
What is a 10:00/km walk in miles?
16:06/mile — walking paces convert by the same factor; nobody is safe from the mile being longer.
Do seconds round up or down?
To the nearest second. Over a marathon the rounding is worth less than one stride.
My watch shows pace in one, my plan in another.
Convert the plan once and tape it to the watch's world — mid-run arithmetic is how workouts die.
